summary: Kyoko Fujii studied at the University of Tokyo (~1967–1977). A scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology, she held professorships at Yokohama City University (1990), Hamamatsu University (1996), Hokkaido University (~1998–2008), and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2008–2019).
Specializing in Buddhist studies and Sinology, Kyoko Tokuno held posts at the University of Oregon and the University of Washington, where she was attested as a professor in 2017.
Kyoshi Renja is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed late-stage doctoral studies (attested 2013) and held a research student post at Taisho University.

Kyosho Hayashima (1914–1999) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. Attested as a lecturer at Yokohama City University and associate professor at Toyo University in 1962, he later served as professor at the University of Tokyo (attested 1980) and taught Shinjo Kawasaki.
Kyosho Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1966–1975). He served as an associate professor at Musashino University from circa 1975 to 2017.
Kyoshun Todo (1916–2002) was a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Bukkyo University, where he served as an assistant professor (attested 1962) and as a professor (attested 1988–1992).
Kōdō Yotsuya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed an MA at Komazawa University and earned a PhD from the University of Hamburg.
Kōichi Furusaka, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied under Hakuyu Hadano. He served as a professor at Osaka Kyoiku University (attested 1991).
Laeticia Söderman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at the University of Helsinki, earning an M.A. by 2010 and continuing as a graduate student (attested 2014).

Lal Mani Joshi (1935–1984) studied at Allahabad, BHU, and Gorakhpur under Govind Chandra Pande. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religion, he taught at Haverford College (~1983–1984) and mentored John W. Pettit and Nawang Tsering Shakspo.
Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi worked in Indology, serving as Jain Pandit at Baroda Central Library and holding an appointment at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1939).

Lama Palden Drolma is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology practitioner who studied under traditional teachers including Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Jamgön Kongtrül III, Bokar Rinpoche, Situ Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, Druptop Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, and Khenpo Tsültrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.
Lama Yeshe Gyamtso is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers Lama Norlha and Kalu Rinpoche (attested 1996).

Lambert Schmithausen studied under Erich Frauwallner and Paul Hacker. A specialist in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, he was a professor at Münster (~1970–1976) and Hamburg (1973–2005; emeritus attested 2013–2014), training numerous prominent scholars.

Lance E. Nelson, an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar, earned his doctorate at McMaster University (1986). He served as a professor at the University of San Diego (attested 1997) and taught James Blumenthal.

Lance S. Cousins (1942–2015) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He served as president of the Pali Text Society (~1994–2002) and held posts at Manchester (attested 1996), Wolfson College, and Oxford (~1995–2015), teaching Sarah Shaw and Rupert Gethin.

Lang Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD at Yale University (attested 2015), where she was supervised by Koichi Shinohara and Phyllis Granoff, and studied under Janet Gyatso.

Lang Eun Ra is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who pursued doctoral studies at Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu, also studying with Bibhuti S. Yadav, Norbert M. Samuelson, and Leonard Swidler.
Lara Braitstein is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and later taught Alnis Dickson.

Larry DeVries earned a PhD from the University of Minnesota and worked in Indology and religious studies. He taught at Minnesota, Hawaii, and Washington, held a research post at Chicago, and was affiliated with Langara College (attested 2005).
